question: How can the Mother of letters both unfold supreme knowledge and still delude even an advanced practitioner?
premises: The supreme Lord's inherent power of reflexive awareness unfolds as will, knowledge, and action.
As supreme speech, this same power becomes the Mother of letters and operates within all knowers through sound and cognition.
When its uncontracted nature is veiled, the letter-powers called Māheśvarī and others bind heedless beings through differentiated knowledge.
inference: Therefore the Mother of letters is the single divine power that can either sustain recognition of pure knowledge or, through heedlessness, produce bondage.

plain_english: Kṣemarāja explains that the same divine power, which is the Lord's own reflexive awareness, unfolds as will, knowledge, and action. As supreme speech it becomes the Mother of letters and works inside every knower, shaping both subtle and gross experience. When a person becomes heedless, the powers of the letters veil the free nature of consciousness and draw one into contracted, divided experience. For this reason, even someone who has reached pure knowledge must remain attentive in all states.
